items.abstract: Knowledge components (KCs) are central to personalizing learning in adaptive systems, providing the unit through which student mastery is modeled and instructional decisions are made. However, constructing KCs is less straightforward in programming education, where a single task can have multiple solutions and a non-compilation error can reflect several possible misconceptions. This property makes it difficult to assign KCs to tasks a priori. While prior bottom-up approaches to automated KC discovery derive components from problem content such as questions or correct solutions, such an approach misses the possibility of students encountering challenges not initially anticipated during task design. This study proposes instead deriving KCs from the natural-language feedback that large language models generate in response to student errors. We present a bottom-up pipeline that embeds and clusters these feedback messages, labels the resulting clusters using GPT-5, validates the labels with a human coder, and evaluates the extracted components in a Bayesian Knowledge Tracing model. Applied to 9,797 student-feedback interactions drawn from an introductory C# programming course with 227 students, the pipeline identified 277 KCs. Human validation of the 50 most frequent KCs indicated that the generated labels accurately characterized the associated feedback messages, and the resulting knowledge-tracing model showed a moderate ability to predict future performance on held-out student dataset. These findings indicate that LLM-generated feedback can serve as a viable and scalable signal for constructing interpretable KC models, offering a new pathway for grounding adaptive learning systems directly in the difficulties students encounter in practice.
title: Beyond compiler errors: An LLM-assisted, bottom-up approach to distilling knowledge components from LLM-generated feedback
